_readme: RemoteOps Q1 demo fixture. Loaded by `make seed` after db/schema.sql + db/reference.sql.
Timestamps are RELATIVE offsets resolved against now() at load time, so the fixture never
goes stale and grants never silently expire. Formats: '-2h', '-30m', '+7d', 'now'.
PASSWORDS: the 'seedPassword' field is plaintext on purpose. The loader MUST hash it on
insert; do not store this value in users.password_hash. One value for everyone so nobody
HIDDEN TESTS MUST NOT READ THIS FILE. It is published, so any hidden test built on a
published id is special-casable. Hidden tests mint their own randomized orgs and tear them
down. This fixture exists for the candidate's manual exploration and for the live demo.
_membershipsNote: Dana and Sam belong to BOTH orgs with different roles. That is the demo: one login, two
Dana: owner in Acme, viewer in Globex  -> the dramatic case
Sam:  operator in Acme, auditor in Globex -> the INVERSION, and the better demo
In Acme Sam can control devices but cannot read the audit log. In Globex she can read the
audit log but cannot control anything. One person, and the two locked items swap. This is
PERMISSIONS.md D2 made visible on a single screen: roles are bundles, not levels.
_grantsNote: Four grants, each seeded to demonstrate a different rule. Together they cover the whole
resolution algorithm, so a candidate can see every rule in the UI on first boot.
1. D3 + D6  grant WIDENS past the role, scoped to ONE device
2. D1 + D4  explicit DENY narrows the role, scoped to one device
3. D1       org-wide DENY beats the role baseline everywhere in the org
4. D6       device-scoped grant: unlocked on exactly one row, locked on all the others

grants._demonstrates: D3 + D6 — a viewer cannot start sessions by role, but can on THIS device only. Because mode=view needs session:start + device:view, they get a working View button on lab-mac-01 and nowhere else.
D1 + D4 — the role grants device:view, this deny removes it. Per PERMISSIONS.md §2, denying device:view removes the row from the list entirely, so kiosk-lobby-01 does not appear for this user at all.

D1 — operator's baseline includes device:terminal; this org-wide deny removes it everywhere in Acme. Sam can still control devices; she just cannot open a shell. Vector 7 in PERMISSIONS.md §11: an org-wide deny is NOT carved out by any device-scoped allow.
D6 — Dana is a viewer in Globex, so Control is locked on every row EXCEPT this one. The clearest single demonstration that authorization is device-scoped rather than org-level.

sessions._demonstrates: PERMISSIONS.md §7.1 — authorized_by is a snapshot. If Sam's grants change now, this session keeps running; only the next one is blocked. Note terminal is denied org-wide for Sam, but this is a control session, so it is unaffected.
A grant-authorized session in the history, so the session list and the audit log are not empty on first boot.

auditEvents._demonstrates: Denied attempts are audited too (invariant 10). Candidates routinely only log successes.
